answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding one identity to one burned fuse inside a certified TPM. The manufacturer burns a fuse per chip and signs its endorsement key; the ledger rejects duplicate keys, so labels like violet, yarrow, or hollow gain no extra slots. The key is non-exportable, so one chip cannot be split. Each extra identity needs another chip costing C, total reward n(R-C), deterring only while R<C. Trust requires the manufacturer never signs duplicate keys; a public certificate log lets anyone audit that.
